title: Mid-Market Account Executive
descriptionHtml:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

 

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

 

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

 

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Responsibilities:

  • You’ll manage complex sales cycles with some of the best mid-market businesses out there, from mid six-figure through to seven-figure+ deals.

  • Multi-thread within accounts and build executive-level relationships, including VP and C-level stakeholders.

  • Most opportunities will be sourced for you by the SDR team and Growth team, however sourcing additional pipeline is expected.

  • You’ll collaborate with the wider team on GTM strategy as we expand our ICP & experiment in other verticals.

  • You’ll help to create our sales processes as you build them.

  • You’ll become the best person in the company at explaining & pitching the product.

  • You’ll work closely with product, engineering, and customer success, bringing in insights from across the company and performing an essential part of our product feedback loop.

Your Traits:

  • Entrepreneurial: creative, resourceful.

  • Executive presence: You are comfortable engaging VPs, CROs, CIOs, and senior RevOps leaders.

  • All-in: hard-working, excited to stretch yourself, willing to take out the trash.

  • Clear thinker, good writer: you can crisply articulate your ideas, goals, and plans and help our customers make sense of hairy consulting-like problems.

Essential Qualifications:

  • 2-5 years of experience.

  • At least 1 year consistently closing deals worth $50k+/year in a multi-stakeholder sales process, consistently hitting six- to seven-figure targets.

  • Ability to execute on a consultative, solutions-oriented, value-based selling methodology (MEDDPICC).

  • Track record of consistent over-achievement in past sales roles.

  • Ability to discuss technical concepts with prospective customers and translate requirements into a demonstrable product.

  • Comfort negotiating and navigating contracts, security and legal discussions without support.

  • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal skills.

Nice-To-Have:

  • Startup/scale-up experience is a plus.

  • Experience selling to Revenue Operations, GTM and/or Sales teams.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce.

What We Offer

We will do our best to offer you a ride of a lifetime. It will not be easy, but it will be thrilling.

  • 🗓️ 24 days holiday per year + bank holidays

  • 🎉 Team events and dinners

  • 🚀 Work directly with the founders to scale the systems that power enterprise AI

  • 🏆 High-autonomy, high-trust environment with a small team shipping at pace

Interview Process

Stage 1 – 30-minute intro call with Talent Partner. You’ll discuss your sales experience and motivations.

Stage 2 – 1-hour interview with Head of Sales. You’ll deep dive into your experience, sales targets & achievements, and Mid-Market AE at Kernel.

Stage 3 – Discovery role play (≤ 2 hours prep).

title: ML Engineer - Internship
descriptionHtml:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

We are looking for a motivated Machine Learning Engineer Intern to join our Data & AI team and contribute to the development of our end-to-end ML pipelines.

You will help improve how we train, evaluate and deploy computer vision models, working on internal AI infrastructure and model lifecycle management.

This internship is ideal for someone interested in applied machine learning, computer vision and MLOps, who wants to gain hands-on experience building reliable AI systems for real-world defence applications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Model training: Improve and optimise training pipelines for computer vision tasks, including object detection, segmentation and tracking.

  • Model evaluation: Develop evaluation frameworks using standard metrics such as mAP, IoU, precision and recall, and automate experiment tracking.

  • Data management: Build reproducible workflows for dataset versioning, augmentation and preprocessing of large-scale image and video datasets.

  • Model deployment: Contribute to deployment workflows for optimised AI models running on edge devices and embedded systems.

Candidate Profile

  • Familiarity with experiment tracking tools such as MLflow or Weights & Biases, and/or data versioning tools such as DVC.

  • Understanding of Docker, Git and cloud platforms such as AWS or GCP.

  • Ability to work autonomously in a research and prototyping environment.

  • Strong collaboration skills and an interest in working in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

title: Model Developer (Client Education)
descriptionHtml:
Hi 👋 I’m Dom Allgood, Client Education Manager at hyperexponential. I joined four years ago as a Curriculum Developer and have spent the last couple of years growing Client Education into the (soon to be) five-person team it is today. Before hx I spent a decade teaching Computing in secondary schools. Outside of work most of my time goes to my two children, and what's left to running and, more recently, mountain biking - where I'm still very much a beginner.

Client Education exists to get our customers to value as quickly as possible, and to keep them there. We run instructor-led training, own hx Academy where all our self-paced learning content lives, own the certification programme, and run some of our customer events. We've also recently taken ownership of Developer+, and that's where this role comes in. Our first customers are working through the programme now, and as it grows it will need to evolve based on what we learn from them.

This isn't a typical Delivery Engineer role, you'll sit in Client Education rather than Delivery Engineering. You'll still work closely with the wider Delivery Engineering team, but your day to day is the customers on Developer+: delivering workshops, running drop-ins, reviewing their code, and shaping the programme around what you learn doing it. You'll partner with Product too, so customers can adopt new enhancements quickly and smoothly. There's no established playbook for this yet, so what matters most is the drive to build one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to own, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we’re building the AI-powered platform that enables the world’s most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes, like whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We’re changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we’re scaling globally. We’re already trusted by nearly 50 of the world’s largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do, from building the world’s first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn’t tied to title or tenure. It’s defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you’ll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Delivery Engineering team

The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that). We specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do.

The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. You’ll uncover every trick in the book, the secret combinations, and the shortcuts. You’ll combine all of this with a growing knowledge of insurance technology to present 'the art of the possible' to our customers and help shape cutting-edge tech, while working alongside some of the brightest, most ambitious people in the tech and insurance industries.

What you'll be doing

  • Move customer teams from hx-led build to independent delivery, shifting effort from pairing toward review and advisory.

  • Keep every engagement moving to its prescribed path, sequencing services to each customer's build stage.

  • Deliver structured enablement sessions; architecture, coding best practice, testing and deployment, model lifecycles.

  • Run code review as a consistent, standards-anchored service, evolving hx's model development standards where reviews expose gaps.

  • Provide drop-in support shaped by each customer's build stage, resolving most issues in session rather than escalating.

  • Make Developer+ repeatable rather than personality-dependent, documenting delivery and using AI to scale capacity.

  • Convert delivery knowledge into hx Academy content, prioritised by what reviews and drop-ins actually surface.

  • Act as the technical voice of the customer into Product, feeding back recurring friction on a regular rhythm.

What you'll need to have done

  • Shipped and maintained production-grade Python code in complex or data-heavy environments, including testing, deployment and model lifecycles.

  • Have excellent pricing and modelling judgement when working with customer’s - working with insurance & actuarial teams is a plus.

  • Developed strong technical enablement instincts, pitching sessions and documentation at the audience's real level.

  • Coached customer teams to work independently rather than solving problems for them.

  • Operated with high ownership and self-direction, building repeatable process where none exists.

  • Prioritised transparently across competing delivery, review and content demands.

  • Communicated with credibility and clarity across developers, actuaries, delivery partners and internal stakeholders.

How we build in an AI-forward company

hx is a maximally AI-forward company because we believe AI should amplify what exceptional people can achieve. Everyone here is a builder. That means staying close to what’s changing, continuing to learn, and using AI to raise the quality, pace and ambition of your work.

We expect everyone to actively experiment with AI and agentic systems, whether at work or in their personal lives. This means going beyond prompting, exploring what agents can do autonomously, and learning by doing. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to be curious, hands-on and willing to push what's possible.

Your current environment is context, not the answer. We’re interested in how you think about what should be possible now, not simply how things are done where you work today. We care about judgement, creativity and ownership, not simply using more tools.

The bar is simple: your work should be meaningfully better because of how you operate in this new world.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  • Talent Team Interview

  • Take-home Python challenge followed by Skills Interview

  • Manager Interview

  • Values Interview

  • Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

Please note that background checks will be conducted as part of the hiring process to ensure compliance with our governance policies. We handle all background checks sensitively and in full compliance with relevant regulations. All applicant data will be processed in accordance with data protection regulations and our privacy policy.

title: Nachwuchsberater (M/W/D)
descriptionHtml:
Über uns

Diagnostik & Künstliche Intelligenz | Organisationsentwicklung

Sie möchten nicht nur analysieren, sondern verstehen, was Menschen und Organisationen wirklich bewegt?

Wie werden aus guten Führungskräften erfolgreiche Führungsteams? Was macht Organisationen zukunftsfähig? Wie lassen sich Persönlichkeit, Führungspotenzial und Zusammenarbeit fundiert beurteilen? Und wie kann künstliche Intelligenz dabei helfen, bessere Erkenntnisse und Entscheidungen zu ermöglichen?

Mit diesen und vielen weiteren Fragestellungen beschäftigen wir uns bei PILLONG.

PILLONG verbindet anspruchsvolle Personal- und Managementberatung mit neuen Perspektiven auf Menschen, Führung und Organisationen.

Wir begleiten Unternehmen und Führungskräfte in komplexen Veränderungsprozessen und entwickeln unsere Beratungsansätze kontinuierlich weiter – insbesondere durch die Verbindung systemischer Organisationsberatung, wissenschaftlich fundierter Diagnostik und moderner KI-Anwendungen.

Dabei setzen wir auf analytische Kompetenz, eigenständiges Denken und die Überzeugung, dass technologische Innovation und menschliche Urteilskraft gemeinsam die Qualität zukünftiger Beratung bestimmen.

Wir verstehen Weiterentwicklung nicht nur als Aufgabe gegenüber unseren Mandanten, sondern als eigenen Anspruch. Deshalb investieren wir gezielt in neue Kompetenzen, Methoden und Menschen, die unsere weitere Entwicklung mitgestalten möchten.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir im Rahmen dieser Weiterentwicklung eine analytisch starke, neugierige und engagierte Nachwuchspersönlichkeit (m/w/d), die gemeinsam mit uns die Zukunft anspruchsvoller Beratung gestalten möchte.

Ihre Aufgaben

Sie arbeiten unmittelbar mit erfahrenen Beratern an anspruchsvollen Mandaten und gewinnen Einblicke in die Herausforderungen von Geschäftsführungen, Führungsteams und Organisationen.

Dabei übernehmen Sie schrittweise eigene Verantwortung.

Ihre Aufgaben umfassen insbesondere:

  • Mitarbeit bei der Anwendung und Weiterentwicklung wissenschaftlich fundierter diagnostischer Instrumente zur Beurteilung von Persönlichkeit, Potenzial und Führungskompetenz

  • Vorbereitung, Auswertung und strukturierte Aufbereitung von Analyse- und Diagnostikergebnissen

  • Aktive Nutzung moderner KI-Anwendungen zur Unterstützung von Research, Analyse, Konzeptentwicklung und Dokumentation unter Beachtung unserer Qualitäts- und Datenschutzstandards

  • Beobachtung wissenschaftlicher und technologischer Entwicklungen sowie Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung neuer diagnostischer und KI-gestützter Beratungsansätze

  • Analyse von Unternehmensstrukturen, Führungsmodellen, Organisationskulturen und Veränderungsprozessen

  • Mitarbeit an Beratungsprojekten in den Bereichen Organisationsentwicklung, Führung, Change Management und Executive Coaching

  • Unterstützung bei der Konzeption und Durchführung von Workshops, Managementinterviews und Beratungsformaten

  • Mitarbeit in anspruchsvollen Executive-Search-Mandaten und bei der Weiterentwicklung bestehender Mandantenbeziehungen

Das bringen Sie mit

Wir suchen keine fertige Beraterpersönlichkeit.

Wir suchen jemanden, der das Potenzial, die Neugier und den persönlichen Anspruch mitbringt, sich zu einer solchen Persönlichkeit zu entwickeln.

Sie überzeugen uns durch:

  • Ein erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium, vorzugsweise in Psychologie, Wirtschaftspsychologie, Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Sozialwissenschaften oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung

  • Ausgeprägtes analytisches und konzeptionelles Denkvermögen sowie Freude daran, komplexe Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen

  • Besonderes Interesse an wissenschaftlich fundierter Diagnostik, psychologischen Methoden und der Beurteilung menschlicher Potenziale

  • Sehr gute digitale Kompetenzen und praktische Erfahrung im reflektierten Einsatz generativer KI-Anwendungen

  • Bereitschaft, neue Technologien kritisch zu hinterfragen und deren Möglichkeiten für anspruchsvolle Beratungsprozesse weiterzuentwickeln

  • Echtes Interesse an Menschen, Führung, Organisationsentwicklung und systemischen Zusammenhängen

  • Hohe Lernbereitschaft, Eigeninitiative, Zuverlässigkeit und einen ausgeprägten Qualitätsanspruch

  • Sehr gute kommunikative Fähigkeiten, Empathie sowie ein sicheres und verbindliches Auftreten

Erste praktische Erfahrungen in der Unternehmensberatung, Personalentwicklung, Diagnostik oder in HR-Projekten sind willkommen, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Wichtiger als ein bereits perfekter Lebenslauf sind uns Ihre intellektuelle Neugier, Ihre Persönlichkeit und Ihr Anspruch an die Qualität Ihrer eigenen Arbeit.

Das bieten wir Ihnen

Wir bieten Ihnen die Möglichkeit, sich in einem etablierten Beratungsunternehmen zu einer qualifizierten und eigenständig handelnden Beraterpersönlichkeit zu entwickeln.

Sie erwartet keine ausschließlich administrative Einstiegsfunktion, sondern die schrittweise Übernahme anspruchsvoller fachlicher Aufgaben.

Sie profitieren von:

  • Unmittelbarer Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und erfahrenen Beratern

  • Fundierter Einarbeitung in diagnostische Methoden und deren professionelle Anwendung

  • Aktiver Mitwirkung an der Integration künstlicher Intelligenz in moderne Beratungsprozesse

  • Praxisnaher Entwicklung in systemischer Organisationsberatung, Managementberatung und Executive Coaching

  • Eigenständigen Projekten und wachsenden Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten

  • Unterstützung bei fachlicher Weiterbildung sowie beim Aufbau eigener Beratungskompetenz

  • Einem professionellen Umfeld mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen, persönlichen Mandantenbeziehungen und einem hohen Anspruch an Qualität und Verlässlichkeit

Sie entwickeln sich mit uns weiter – und bringen zugleich Ihre eigenen Ideen und Perspektiven in die Weiterentwicklung unseres Unternehmens ein.

Unser Ziel ist eine langfristige Zusammenarbeit, in der Sie fachlich und persönlich wachsen und zunehmend eigenständige Beratungsverantwortung übernehmen.

Sie möchten sich mit uns weiterentwickeln?

Dann freuen wir uns darauf, Sie kennenzulernen.

Uns interessiert nicht nur, was Sie bisher gemacht haben, sondern vor allem, welche Themen Sie bewegen, wie Sie denken und wie Sie die Verbindung von menschlicher Beratung, wissenschaftlicher Diagnostik und künstlicher Intelligenz sehen.

title: Non-linear Analyses Mechanical Engineer

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with partners to drive success of OneStream implementations and partner success.

title: People Operations Manager, UK
descriptionHtml:
TL;DR: Own Lovable’s UK People Operations, from payroll and commissions to benefits and day-to-day employee support. You’ll be a hands-on operator and a trusted point of contact for our London team, partnering with a coordinated global People Ops function to deliver reliable, people-first experiences. You’ll use data, systems and AI to make the work more scalable without losing the human touch.

This is an in-office role, five days a week.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we’re looking for

  • 5–6+ years in UK People Operations or HR, with hands-on ownership of UK payroll, commissions and employee benefits.

  • Strong operational judgment and attention to detail: you can keep complex processes accurate and on time, handle sensitive information with care, and know when to bring in specialists.

  • An analytical mindset and a track record of using data to spot issues and improve how work gets done.

  • Clear, empathetic communication and the confidence to influence without authority, challenge constructively and work through trade-offs with senior stakeholders.

  • A team-first, hands-on approach and the ability to take ownership in a fast-moving, changing environment. You’re excited to be in our London office five days a week.

  • Experience with or strong interest in building automations, workflows and AI agents in People Operations.

  • Preferred: Experience in a startup or high-growth environment, including scaling beyond 500 employees; exposure to European labor law or multi-country operations; or experience implementing HR systems and automation.

What you’ll do

  • Own UK payroll and commissions: Coordinate inputs, checks and handoffs to ensure accurate, timely delivery, resolve exceptions and improve processes as the business grows.

  • Run UK benefits: Own implementation, administration and employee communications in partnership with our Head of Total Rewards.

  • Support immigration and compliance: Coordinate UK immigration processes with our mobility and immigration team, and help keep local People policies and operations running smoothly.

  • Support our people: Be a primary point of contact for the UK team, providing responsive, thoughtful support and making moments like onboarding, payroll and benefits feel effortless.

  • Improve how work gets done: Use data to identify trends and operational issues, and design automations, workflows and AI agents that reduce manual work while protecting employee data and trust.

  • Partner across the business: Work with Finance and global People Ops on reporting, audits, systems and process improvements. Help senior stakeholders navigate people-related decisions, objections and trade-offs.

How you’ll fit in

  • With global People Ops: You’ll own UK delivery while collaborating closely with a coordinated global team and contributing to international initiatives, especially around systems and tooling.

  • With specialist partners: You’ll work with Total Rewards on benefits and with mobility and immigration specialists on UK cases, bringing the right people in when their expertise is needed.

  • As a builder: You’ll keep the day-to-day running reliably while finding practical ways to make existing processes simpler and more scalable. Automation should free up time for the moments when people need a human.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

descriptionHtml:

An unseren zwei Standorten in Hamburg und Wiesbaden entwickeln, integrieren und betreiben wir IT-Lösungen für Unternehmen aus Handel, Versicherung, Medien und Industrie.

Zu unseren langjährigen Kunden zählen unter anderem OTTO, R+V Versicherung, Allianz Trade und Suzuki.

Aufgaben

RPA bedeutet: Software-Roboter übernehmen manuelle, repetitive Aufgaben in digitalen Systemen – zum Beispiel das automatische Anlegen, Bearbeiten oder Löschen von Einträgen in einem CMS oder die automatisierte Ausspielung von Beiträgen im Intranet. Für einen unserer Konzernkunden bauen wir genau das aktuell auf: RPA-Lösungen für Marketing und Unternehmenskommunikation, weil die eingesetzten Systeme keine klassischen Schnittstellen bieten.

Du suchst einen Praktikumsplatz, in dem du von Anfang an in ein echtes Kundenprojekt einsteigst, mit modernen Automatisierungstools arbeitest und dabei wirklich etwas bewegst? Dann wird DIU interessant für dich. Bei uns gibt es keine politischen Abstimmungen und langen Wege – transparent, professionell, intelligent. Als Praktikant (m/w/d) RPA-Automatisierung im Marketing arbeitest du aktiv am Aufbau der RPA-Lösung für unseren Kunden mit: Du modellierst Automatisierungsprozesse in Blue Prism, verstehst Prozesslogik und bringst dich bei Code Reviews mit dem RPA-Team des Kunden ein.

Wir suchen dich für ein Vollzeit-Praktikum von 3–6 Monaten – remote oder mit optionaler Präsenz in Hamburg, wo wir uns derzeit etwa einmal wöchentlich im Büro treffen. Du arbeitest eng mit einer erfahrenen Integratorin zusammen, die dich einarbeitet und begleitet, und bist von Beginn an Teil unseres MarTech-Teams an den Standorten Hamburg und Wiesbaden. Für Studierende mit Leidenschaft fürs Thema besteht nach dem Praktikum die Möglichkeit zur Weiterbeschäftigung als Werkstudent:in.

  • Du überführst Automatisierungsanforderungen aus dem Kundenbriefing in Blue-Prism-Prozesse und entwickelst sie bis zur lauffähigen Lösung.

  • Du pflegst und erweiterst bestehende Blue-Prism-Workflows und bringst dich aktiv in die laufende Lösungsentwicklung ein.

  • Du nutzt KI-gestützte Tools wie Claude und MCP-Server als ergänzendes Werkzeug im Projektalltag.

  • Du arbeitest mit CMS-Systemen und verstehst, wie Schnittstellen funktionieren – auch dort, wo APIs fehlen.

  • Du nimmst an Code Reviews mit dem RPA-Entwicklerteam des Kunden teil und verstehst, was hinter den Code Stages steckt.

  • Du dokumentierst Prozesse, Workflows und Lösungsansätze strukturiert für Team und Kunden.

  • Du testest automatisierte Prozesse, analysierst Fehler und bringst Verbesserungen ein.

  • Du stimmst dich regelmäßig mit dem Team und den Ansprechpartner:innen beim Kunden ab.

Qualifikation

KNOWHOW

  • Laufendes Studium der Wirtschaftsinformatik, Informationswissenschaft, Digital Business oder eines vergleichbaren technisch-digitalen Studiengangs.

  • Interesse an Prozessautomatisierung und Lust, dich schnell in Blue Prism einzuarbeiten; erste Erfahrungen mit RPA oder ähnlichen Automatisierungstools sind von Vorteil.

  • Verständnis für digitale Systemlandschaften und Schnittstellen; Erfahrungen mit APIs, Middlewares oder CMS-Systemen sind ein Plus.

  • Offenheit für KI-gestützte Tools wie Claude und MCP-Server – oder bereits erste Erfahrungen damit.

  • Strukturierte, lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise und die Fähigkeit, auch in einem laufenden Projekt schnell mitzudenken.

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Benefits

DIU FOR YOU

Bei DIU besetzen wir nicht Stellen, sondern suchen nach Menschen mit Leidenschaft für ihr Fachgebiet. Wir verstehen uns als Plattform für ein Team aus Menschen, die ihre Leidenschaft mit anderen teilen oder in Projekte einbringen möchten. Den Rahmen für diese Arbeit schaffen wir mit:

descriptionHtml:
Wir suchen Dich als Pricing & Packaging Senior Lead (x/f/m) für unser Revenue Operations Team in Berlin.

Du entwickelst Preisentscheidungen auf Basis von Zahlungsbereitschaft, Wettbewerb und Unit Economics, vertrittst sie gegenüber dem Leadership und sorgst dafür, dass sie im Markt so ankommen, wie sie gedacht sind: im Angebot der Seller:innen, in den Rabattregeln und im realisierten Preis.

Deine Aufgaben

title: Principal Connectivity Planner
descriptionHtml:
About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

The role

As Principal Connectivity Planner, you will be Volta's planning authority for network connectivity. You will own the integrated connectivity plan across the portfolio, linking carrier services, long-haul routes, Data Center Connectivity Infrastructure, network equipment installation and turn-up to compute capacity dates.

This is a principal-level individual contributor role, reporting to the Senior Director, Global Network Connectivity Delivery. Your forecasts will be what leadership relies on to commit capacity dates, and your planning standards will be used by every connectivity workstream and supplier.

What you will do

Integrated planning

  • Own the global integrated connectivity schedule, aligned to the master, commissioning and deployment schedules.

  • Set Volta's connectivity planning standards: work breakdown, coding, durations, progress rules and reporting.

  • Lead program schedule reviews and analytics, analyzing data and executing reports to ensure project schedules are aligned

  • Lead contractor schedule reviews as required with sites to ensure consistent delivery of connectivity and network Infrastructure across Voltas Sites.

Risk and recovery

Capability and improvement

  • Use actual delivery data to set benchmark durations and improve supplier forecasts.

  • Strong understanding of carrier lead times, fibre delivery, equipment installation and activation.

  • Credibility with senior leadership when forecasting dates and recommending recovery options.

Nice to have

  • Background managing Long-haul fibre, permits and carrier provisioning programmes.

title: Principal Consultant (Senior Manager) - Operational Resilience & Cyber
descriptionHtml:
Principal Consultant (Senior Manager) – Operational Resilience & Cyber Risk

Location: Edinburgh or Glasgow (Hybrid) | Practice Area: Finance, Risk, Regulatory & Financial Crime | Type: Permanent

Build resilience where it matters most across cyber, technology, and third-party risk

The Role

Capco is seeking experienced Principal Consultants in Operational Resilience and Cyber Risk to join our growing Finance, Risk, Regulatory & Financial Crime (FRRF) capability. In this senior role, you'll lead client engagements across financial services and energy, advising on regulatory expectations such as PRA requirements and DORA while supporting the design and implementation of effective resilience frameworks.

You'll play a key role in shaping client strategy, overseeing transformation programmes and contributing to capability growth. Working collaboratively with clients and multidisciplinary teams, you'll help strengthen operational resilience, improve risk management and deliver sustainable transformation outcomes aligned with regulatory expectations and business priorities.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead operational resilience assessments, scenario testing and control implementation programmes, identifying opportunities to strengthen resilience outcomes and improve operational effectiveness.

  • Advise clients on regulatory readiness across PRA requirements, DORA and other resilience frameworks, translating regulatory expectations into practical transformation strategies and sustainable operating models.

  • Oversee cyber risk, third-party risk and vendor resilience assessments, using data-driven insights and professional judgement to strengthen risk identification, prioritisation and decision-making.

  • Design and implement governance models, dashboards, Important Business Services (IBS), Impact Tolerance (ITOL) frameworks and reporting mechanisms, ensuring effective oversight, control assurance and regulatory alignment.

  • Lead cyber and technology resilience transformation initiatives, including tooling, cloud security and control enhancements, while contributing to business development, proposition development and capability growth.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience delivering operational resilience, cyber risk and third-party risk transformation within financial services, energy or management consulting.

  • Understanding of regulatory frameworks, including PRA requirements, DORA and related operational resilience standards.

  • Experience leading transformation programmes, including scenario testing, IBS/ITOL calibration, control remediation and operating model transformation.

  • Experience assessing operational and technology risks, developing practical resilience solutions and supporting effective governance, control implementation and regulatory compliance.

  • Effective communication, leadership and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage senior stakeholders across business and technology functions.

Bonus Points For

  • Experience leading enterprise-wide operational resilience or cyber transformation programmes.

  • Background in cloud security, cyber tooling implementation or cyber security architecture.

  • Experience with vendor risk management, third-party governance, supply chain resilience and remediation strategies.

  • Experience mentoring, coaching and developing consulting teams.

  • Experience contributing to business development, proposition development and strategic client growth.

Why Join Capco

  • Deliver high-impact transformation programmes for Tier 1 financial institutions.

  • Work in a collaborative, flat, and entrepreneurial consulting culture.

  • Access continuous learning, industry certifications, and structured leadership development.

  • Help shape the future of cyber and operational resilience through innovation, automation, and technology.

  • Be part of a team delivering meaningful change across financial services and energy.

Benefits

We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life:

  • Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover.

  • Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders.

  • Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement.

  • Family Care: 8 complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care.

  • Holiday Flexibility: 5 weeks of annual leave with the option to buy or sell holiday days based on your needs.

  • Continuous Learning: Your growth, your way – minimum 40 hours of training annually. Take your pick: workshops, certifications, e-learning. Also, Business Coach assigned from Day One: Get one-on-one guidance to fast-track your goals and accelerate your development.

title: Product Engineer - AI Neobank
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

The Role

We are looking for product engineers to own product areas within Doit's AI Neobank.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

 

What You'll Own

  • Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

  • Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

  • Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

  • Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

  • Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

  • Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

  • Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

 

What We're Looking For

  • Experience as Product Engineer, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

  • Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

  • Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

  • Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

  • Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

  • High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

 

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

  • Can make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

  • Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

  • Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

 

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

  • PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

  • Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

  • People who launch features and then stop caring.

  • PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

 

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Germany.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Product Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default

Founded in 2014 by scientists who met at CERN, Proton was built on the belief that privacy is a fundamental human right. What started as an encrypted email service has grown into an ecosystem of privacy-first products, including Proton Mail, VPN, Drive, Pass, and Calendar, used by millions of people worldwide.

We're profitable, independent, and building for the long term. Free from venture capital control and advertising-driven business models, we focus on what matters most: our users. Our work helps protect digital freedom, from everyday privacy to supporting journalists and activists in challenging environments.

Today, we're an international team of 700+ people, with offices across 9 countries. We have high standards for the people we hire and the work we do. You'll work alongside talented, driven colleagues who challenge each other, take ownership, and care about getting things right.

Explore our open-source projects.

Your impact:

We’re hiring Product Engineers across different levels of experience, from junior to staff engineers. Whether you’re looking to take the next step in your career or already have experience leading complex technical projects, we’d love to hear from you. Your scope and level will reflect your experience and the impact you can bring.

As a Product Engineer, you’ll help shape what we build and own work from understanding the problem through to release and improvement. You’ll speak directly with customers, collaborate with Product and Design, and work across the parts of the stack needed to deliver a complete solution.

What you will do:

  • Understand and shape the problem: Work with Product, Design and customers to understand user needs, question assumptions and decide what is worth building.
  • Own complete features: Turn problems into practical solutions across clients, services and data. Take work through testing, release and improvement, paying attention to usability, performance and behaviour in production.
  • Build effectively with agents: Define clear tasks, provide context and evaluate generated code. Investigate failures, challenge suggestions and make changes yourself when needed.
  • Improve how software gets built: Turn recurring problems into better agent instructions, tests, tools and automated safeguards. Share improvements that help the whole team.
  • Build for trust: Make privacy, security, reliability and maintainability part of your decisions. Verify important failure cases, communicate what remains uncertain and make sound trade-offs about release readiness.

What you will bring:

  • Experience delivering production software: You can explain the problems you solved, the decisions you made and what you learned from maintaining your work after release.
  • Technical depth and adaptability: You have strong expertise and can contribute beyond it. You don’t need equal expertise in every layer, but you understand how your work interacts with the wider system.
  • Practical capability with coding agents: You’ve used agents to deliver working software and can explain how you guide them, improve unsuccessful approaches and verify their output.
  • Code fluency and engineering judgement: You can navigate unfamiliar code, trace behaviour, diagnose problems and make precise changes. You can assess an implementation regardless of who — or what — wrote it.
  • Product judgement: You connect technical choices to user needs, care about the quality of the experience and distinguish a useful reduction in scope from a shortcut that puts users at risk.
  • Ownership and collaboration: You move work forward through uncertainty, explain trade-offs clearly, seek out expertise and take responsibility for the outcome.
  • Technical leadership: You’ve led complex projects through ambiguous requirements, made decisions with lasting consequences and helped other engineers develop their judgement while remaining hands-on.

What we offer:

  • Work that Matters: Millions of people trust Proton with their privacy. We answer only to our users — not advertisers, not investors with conflicting agendas, not governments.
  • A Great Team: Diverse, collaborative, and tight-knit, with people from MIT, Harvard, Stanford, Caltech, Cambridge, ETH, and more.
  • Technology: The right hardware and software to do your best work.
  • Learning & Development: We invest in your growth. Proton is one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career — real challenges, real ownership, from day one.
  • Employee Benefits: Strong health coverage, solid retirement options, generous leave, and wellness support.
  • Stock Options: From day one, you have a real stake in what we're building. When Proton wins, you win.
  • In-Person Collaboration: Offices across Geneva, Zürich, Barcelona, London, and more. You'll spend most of your time collaborating face-to-face.
  • Food: Lunch and snacks on us every day in the office.
  • Transport: We cover public transport, bike allowances, or parking — whichever works for you.
  • Flexible Working: You own your schedule. Outcomes matter more than clock-in times.

Compensation range:

  • Compensation will be discussed during the interview process.
  • We're hiring across multiple experience levels for this position. Your level and compensation will be determined based on your skills, experience and performance throughout the interview process.

Our commitment to diversity and inclusion:

At Proton, we believe diversity drives innovation and strengthens our mission to provide privacy as a default for all. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where all individuals, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, physical ability, or socio-economic background, feel valued and empowered. We strive to create equal opportunities, promote open dialogue, and support continuous learning to ensure every voice is heard and respected.

If you need any extra support or reasonable adjustments during the hiring process, please let your talent partner know.

Candidate privacy notice:

When you apply for a position, refer a candidate, or are considered for a role at Proton AG ("Proton," "we," "us," or "our"), we store and process your information using Greenhouse, our recruitment platform. Two privacy policies apply to this information, together:

  • Greenhouse's Service Privacy Policy, which governs how Greenhouse, as our data processor, handles and secures the information within their platform.
  • Proton's Recruitment & Hiring Privacy Notice, which governs how we, as the data controller, use, retain, and manage your information.

We use your information to evaluate your suitability for the role you've applied for. We also retain it to consider you for future roles that may align with your background and skills, unless you ask us not to.

Once we no longer have a legitimate business need to process your information, we will delete or anonymize it. If you have questions about how we use or manage your data, or if you'd like to access, correct, or delete it, contact our privacy team at Proton does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from candidates, and we will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from an unsolicited submission, even if the candidate is later hired by Proton.

title: Product Engineer, UK
descriptionHtml:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

This is a product-builder role, not a ticket-taking one. You own a product surface end to end: you talk to the customer, form the idea, build it, ship it, measure it, and decide what happens next. The same person who understands the repairer writes the code. There is no handoff for product quality to leak through.

You'll build at the center of a multi-trillion-dollar industry that still runs on phone calls, spreadsheets, and tribal knowledge. Replacement parts is one of the largest physical markets on earth and one of the least digitised, and there is no established playbook to copy. Partly is creating the category.

Our moat is Interpreter, a domain-specific AI model that understands parts, vehicles, and the messy real-world relationships between them in ways general-purpose models cannot. It is what lets software finally make sense of a physical, offline industry, and it is the engine underneath everything you build.

And what you build is changing shape. We are not bolting AI onto old screens. We are creating genuinely new agentic experiences for a broad spectrum of users, from estimators and parts managers to accountants and suppliers, where people express intent and supervise outcomes while agents handle the mechanical work. Designing how that trust is earned, surface by surface, while each one still delivers value today, is the heart of the role.

You'll work at an inflection point in how software itself gets built. AI-assisted development has collapsed the distance between an idea and a working version of it. The builders we want already work this way: they prototype in an afternoon, put it in front of real customers within days, and read the signal themselves. We want someone who works like that now, or is visibly building toward it.

💻 What will you do

  • Build, not just specify. Prototype new product iterations yourself using AI-assisted and LLM-assisted tooling, fast, disposable, real. Treat the prototype as the hypothesis and put it in front of real customers before writing the spec. Ship production code, instrument it, and watch how it actually gets used.

  • Stay close to customers. Spend time where the work happens. Understand what estimators, parts managers, and others actually do, where they lose time, and what better would feel like. This is a core weekly activity, not an occasional input.

  • Reconcile signal. Combine what you see with what the data says, and reconcile the two when they disagree. Turn that understanding straight into what you build next.

  • Own the outcome. Steer by your surface's metrics; adoption and value delivered are yours. Make the call on priority and explain the reasoning, especially when the answer is no. When something is broken, own it, diagnose it precisely, and fix it.

  • Make the trade-off. Weigh product impact against engineering effort in the same breath, and find the cheaper path to the same outcome.

  • Build the agentic experience. Move your surface from manual operation toward supervised delegation: capture intent, decide where the human stays in the loop, and earn trust step by step so users never lose the thread of a high-stakes job.

  • Hold the craft. The surface feels fast, clear, and considered. You push back when something does not feel right, even when it technically works.

  • Raise the bar. Pair with SW Engineers on the harder systems work behind your surface, and contribute beyond your boundary: shared components, product craft, and what excellent building looks like here as the team grows.

🥷 Your skills

Non-negotiables

  • You ship end to end: a track record of taking features from idea to production, code included, with clear accountability for whether they worked. Roughly 3+ years building and shipping software in production.

  • Genuine customer obsession: a real habit of spending time with users in their work context, with a track record of that depth driving what you build.

  • Product taste and craft: the bar is experiences that feel effortless to time-pressured, non-technical users across fragmented, high-stakes workflows. Functional is not the finish line.

  • A point of view on agentic product design: how an experience moves from manual operation to supervised delegation, and how automation earns user trust gradually rather than all at once.

  • You build rapid prototypes yourself, with AI-assisted tools as a first instinct for testing an idea.

  • Solid full-stack engineering with a frontend lean: production-quality code and sound fundamentals. Systems-specialist depth is not the point of the role.

  • Trade-off fluency: you weigh product impact against engineering effort and often find a cheaper route to the same result.

  • Strong analytical instinct: you define the metric, build the view, read it, and act, without waiting for a data team.

  • You operate well in ambiguity and autonomy, and shape the problem rather than waiting for a spec.

Strong signals we look for

  • Shipped AI-assisted or agent-driven features in production, particularly where the human stays in the loop.

  • Built for a multi-persona, operational, or workflow-heavy B2B product.

  • Founder background, or early employee at a startup that scaled materially.

  • You've killed or radically changed something you personally believed in, and can explain why.

Bonus

  • Domain knowledge in automotive, the parts aftermarket, repair, or insurance claims.

  • Marketplace or network experience, from the demand or supply side.

  • Rust, or genuine eagerness to learn it. It is part of our stack.

Please note: if you don't have all the skills or experience listed above but believe you could be outstanding in this role, please still consider applying. Many people count themselves out. We'd love the chance to learn more about you and why you're exceptional.

🪅Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + equity. We offer competitive salaries and generous equity options for all full-time employees, ensuring everyone shares in the financial upside when we win.

  • Annual global offsite in New Zealand. Travel with the rest of the UK and EU team as we gather and connect for 1-2 weeks at our product and engineering hub in Christchurch.

  • Parental leave: Primary caregivers receive 3 months of fully paid parental leave, plus a flexible return-to-work (four days on full pay for your first three months back).

  • Team lunches: Lunch provided daily (Monday to Friday) in the office

  • Flexible working hours: We have flexible working hours and default to working from the office.

  • Season openers & events: We host regular events, including quarterly "season openers" for our UK/EU team, monthly team catch-ups, and weekly happy hours.

  • Healthy body, healthy mind: Every team member gets a £750 annual wellness allowance on a Partly-branded card. Use on gym memberships, rock climbing, physio, massage, GP visits, prescriptions; anything that you or your family, need.

title: Product Frontend Engineer
descriptionHtml:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app.

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters.

Where this is going

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.

Why this role exists

Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening.

How we work

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own

Everything on the screen:

  • The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.
  • The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.
  • The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.
  • Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.
  • The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins.

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

title: Product Lead - AI Neobank App
descriptionHtml:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

The Role

We are looking for product leads to shape and drive major product areas within Doit's AI Neobank App.

This role is for senior product builders who can own direction, execution, product quality and outcomes across multiple workstreams or squads.

 

What You'll Own

  • Lead product direction for major AI Neobank app areas.

  • Define priorities, roadmap, product standards and success metrics across multiple features or squads.

  • Guide PMs, Product Owners, designers and engineers toward clear execution.

  • Work across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel and other financial services.

  • Turn regulatory, operational and business constraints into practical product decisions.

  • Drive launch quality, post-launch learning and continuous improvement.

  • Help build a product culture focused on speed, clarity, user value and honest measurement.


What We're Looking For

  • Strong experience leading digital product areas, not just individual features.

  • Able to balance strategy, execution, UX, data, engineering and business outcomes.

  • Strong judgement on prioritization, trade-offs and product sequencing.

  • Experience leading or mentoring PMs / POs / cross-functional squads is a strong advantage.

  • Comfortable with high ambiguity, fast changes and senior stakeholder pressure.

  • Able to simplify complex financial products into usable journeys.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or regulated products is a strong advantage.


The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Can set direction and still go deep into details.

  • Pushes teams to move faster without lowering product quality.

  • Knows when to simplify, when to scale and when to say no.

  • Can lead through clarity, not bureaucracy.

  • Avoids false claims and understands that product impact usually comes from many iterations and teams.


This Role Is Not For

  • Product leaders who only manage people and meetings.

  • People who cannot go deep into product details.

  • Candidates who are too slow for a high-growth environment.

  • Leaders who push vanity metrics without understanding real user impact.

  • People who need large teams before they can create progress.


Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Germany.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

 

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Product Manager - Customer Account Lifecycle (CAL) + Market Interactions, Paris (Français & Anglais)
descriptionHtml:
Job title: Product Manager - Customer Account Lifecycle (CAL)

Lieu: Location: Paris, France — (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)

Team: Product Management

Contrat: CDI

Reporting To: Group Product Manager

Merci de noter : ce poste est basé en France, vous devez y résider ou envisager de vous y installer, et il nécessite un droit de travail existant dans l’UE. Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de sponsoring de visa, mais nous étudions cette possibilité poste par poste, alors n’hésitez pas à consulter régulièrement notre site carrières pour découvrir de futures opportunités.

Le français et l’anglais courants (à l’oral comme à l’écrit) sont indispensables, et nous vous remercions de soumettre votre CV en anglais.

À propos de Kaluza

Kaluza est l’Energy Intelligence Platform : nous transformons la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les acteurs de l’énergie à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.

Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel entre les foyers, les équipements, les marchés et les réseaux. En combinant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie de tous les jours.

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des innovateurs comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Ce que vous ferez

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec une équipe d’ingénieurs logiciels sur l’expansion belge de notre domaine Customer Account Lifecycle (CAL), l’un des domaines produit centraux de la plateforme Kaluza. Il gère les informations sur les clients, les comptes et les contrats, et porte les parcours client associés (par exemple un déménagement ou un changement de contrat). C’est un domaine full stack : une interface pour les conseillers du service client, des API qui exposent les données et des services backend qui portent les bases de données et la logique de workflow. Vous travaillez donc sur l’ensemble du domaine produit. Ce n’est pas un poste de product owner : vous portez des fonctionnalités de bout en bout, du dialogue avec les clients et les utilisateurs jusqu’à la livraison du logiciel, en animant le quotidien de l’équipe et la discovery.

Des déplacements ponctuels en Belgique sont possibles (environ deux par trimestre).

  • Traduire les exigences du marché belge en spécifications claires : transformer les règles du marché belge de l’énergie en exigences produit précises.

  • Devenir le partenaire de confiance du client : travailler main dans la main avec ENGIE et les futurs clients du marché belge pour comprendre leurs besoins, mener la discovery en ateliers afin de définir comment le produit fonctionne et de cadrer le périmètre, construire les exigences ensemble et bâtir une relation de confiance telle qu’ils viennent vers vous en premier. Cette proximité vous aide à orienter ce que CAL construira ensuite.

  • Construire, pas seulement spécifier : passer vous-même de l’idée au prototype fonctionnel, en interrogeant les données, en explorant les schémas d’API et en montant des preuves de concept. Nous attendons de vous que vous utilisiez l’IA (par exemple Claude Code) chaque jour comme un multiplicateur pour prototyper, investiguer et débloquer, pas seulement pour rédiger des documents.

  • Aligner les équipes globales et locales sur toutes les fonctions : travailler étroitement avec l’ingénierie, l’UX, le QA et d’autres équipes, avec une influence full stack, en animant le quotidien de l’équipe (priorités, cérémonies, réunions), pour que chacun vise les bons résultats. Vous faites le lien entre les équipes globales et locales pour nourrir les priorités et la stratégie.

Ce que vous apportez

Idéalement, vous avez ou vous êtes :

  • Une expérience avérée de Product Manager, de Business Analyst ou d’un rôle équivalent dans des éditeurs de logiciels, avec un parcours réussi de localisation de produits logiciels complexes pour des marchés internationaux.

  • Un français courant et un anglais professionel : notre plateforme et beaucoup de nos équipes fonctionnent en anglais, et vous passez facilement de l’une à l’autre langue.

  • De l’aisance en direct avec les clients : vous savez animer une session de travail avec des interlocuteurs clients, faire émerger le vrai besoin derrière la demande, et garder les profils seniors alignés et impliqués.

  • Un état d’esprit de bâtisseur et une aisance technique : débrouillard et concret, vous êtes à l’aise pour construire un prototype fonctionnel plutôt que d’attendre la spécification parfaite. Vous êtes à l’aise avec les données et les modèles de données, les bases de données et les API, et vous savez prototyper avec les outils d’IA modernes. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être ingénieur, mais vous pensez comme tel et vous tenez votre place dans une conversation technique. Vous raisonnez aussi bien sur un modèle de données que sur ce que l’utilisateur final voit à l’écran.

  • Une communication claire et incisive, et l’habitude du travail transverse : vous savez aller à l’essentiel et expliquer la complexité technique et marché à des publics variés, clients compris. Vous collaborez avec l’ingénierie, le QA, le BA, le programme, le delivery, etc., pour livrer des solutions localisées.

  • La maîtrise des outils d’IA à toutes les étapes du cycle de vie produit, de la discovery et l’idéation jusqu’à la livraison et l’itération.

Nos valeurs

Cinq valeurs guident notre façon de travailler chez Kaluza :

  • Jouer pour gagner : La fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : Dépasser la complexité pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

  • Bâtir la confiance chaque jour : Cohérence, transparence et tenir parole.

  • Assumer les résultats : Une responsabilité totale, dans les réussites comme dans les revers, sans ego.

  • Aller plus loin ensemble : Collaboration, respect et diversité des points de vue.

Nos avantages

Rémunération & protection : Bonus discrétionnaire, mutuelle Alan, prévoyance (assurance vie et décès) via Alan, et cotisations standard de Sécurité sociale (retraite, allocations familiales, assurance chômage)

Indemnités : Remboursement de 50 % des frais de transport domicile-travail, indemnité de télétravail de 200 € et budget formation de 150 €

Congés & flexibilité : 25 jours de congés + 1 jour pour votre anniversaire + jours fériés + jours de RTT (11), congés « Moments That Matter », congé pour événement familial, deux jours de bénévolat rémunérés, flexibilité dans l’organisation du travail et éligibilité à un congé sabbatique (Career Break)

Venez comme vous êtes

Nous voulons rencontrer des personnes de tous horizons. Plus nous sommes inclusifs, meilleur sera notre travail, et nous reconnaissons les talents sur la base du mérite et du potentiel. Si le poste vous enthousiasme mais que vous ne cochez pas toutes les cases, nous serions quand même ravis de vous lire.

Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur notre careers page et sur LinkedIn. Notre politique de protection des données des candidats est disponible here.

Compensation: €46K – €63K
